promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 糖 (candy / sugar), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet who keeps drifting off the ground, and swirled candies. Soft peach backdrop; the glyph is hot-pink with white stripe highlights. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: a toy astronaut bounces in and begins drifting upward; the voice says the first 糖 as a pink striped candy stroke peeks in from the left edge and zips back out. 1.5-3.0s: another piece sneaks in from the top, one from the right; the astronaut lunges, misses, and spins slowly. The voice says the second 糖 as all pieces dodge him in a round of peekaboo. 3.0-4.5s: he floats upside-down, the pieces tiptoe back behind him and pop into 糖 at 70% of frame height; he lands with a soft bounce. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 糖果 (ㄊㄤˊ ㄍㄨㄛˇ) as wrapped candies rain down and tink off his helmet. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still; the astronaut hovers and catches a candy in a mitten. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 糖、糖、糖果 (ㄊㄤˊ、ㄊㄤˊ、ㄊㄤˊ ㄍㄨㄛˇ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, and stop; no other speech, subtitles or loud music. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 糖 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.
